related_questions.question: Do we have net neutrality right now?

text_blocks.snippet: No, the US does not currently have net neutrality. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) repealed the existing net neutrality rules in 2017, and while there have been attempts to reinstate them, those efforts have been challenged in court. The current legal landscape regarding net neutrality remains uncertain.

list.snippet: The FCC initially adopted net neutrality rules, classifying broadband internet as a public utility and prohibiting blocking, throttling, and paid prioritization of internet traffic.
The FCC, under the Trump administration, repealed these rules.

list.title: Ongoing Legal Challenges:
list.snippet: The repeal has faced legal challenges from various parties, including states and consumer advocacy groups, while the FCC has also attempted to reinstate the rules.

list.title: Current Status:
list.snippet: While the FCC has voted to reinstate the rules and set an effective date, these actions are still subject to legal challenges. A federal appeals court has struck down the FCC's net neutrality rules, creating further uncertainty about the future of net neutrality, according to NPR.

text_blocks.snippet: Therefore, while there is ongoing effort to restore net neutrality, it is not currently in effect.
